canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Current evidence retains one blocker and clears the two gate-related blockers. EV-05-001 remains supported: the strict readiness path only requires ready lower-band text, while strict projection selection rejects the same semantic lower-band chunks when exact detailed/brief counts are absent and can still return ready with empty lower bands. EV-05-002 and EV-05-003 are not retained: the previously disputed lifecycle test and the long-thread real-runtime proof both pass in this workspace, and npm run verify-all completed successfully with 491 service tests, 15 general e2e tests, and all 3 long-thread real PI e2e tests green. Reviewer 2 is therefore correct on gate health and placeholder cutover, but not on the remaining strict-accounting contract drift.
crossStoryFindings: Normal runtime lower-band consumption is now cohesive around semantic chunk.lowerBand artifacts; the active compact/build/materialize path does not use placeholder output as a production fallback.

The remaining cross-story defect is a contract split inside strict mode: lower-band readiness can pass a canonical semantic chunk state that strict projection building then silently omits from detailed/brief output because exact semantic accounting is missing.
architectureFindings: The design and token-accounting surface expose exact/provider-input counting for semantic lower-band artifact text, but the runtime write/repair path never actually supplies those counts to chunk.lowerBand artifacts.

Because strict prepare/readiness checks only artifact text presence while strict projection selection applies strict counter-source policy to detailed/brief accounting, the implementation has two incompatible definitions of what lower-band ready means.

The current test suite codifies this drift instead of failing on it: one service test blesses canonical semantic chunks with no lower-band token metadata, while the strict builder test expects a ready result with empty lower bands for that same chunk shape.
epicCoverageAssessment: Gate coverage is green in the current candidate: npm run verify-all passed, including the previously disputed lifecycle service test and the long-thread real-runtime PI proofs.

Coverage still does not protect the architecture contract for strict semantic lower-band counting; current service/builder tests explicitly allow the readiness/selection mismatch instead of rejecting it.
productionPathFindings: No active placeholder fallback was verified on the production compact/build/materialize path; selected lower-band output is sourced from semantic chunk.lowerBand artifacts and legacy placeholder chunks are blocked.

The remaining production-path defect is counted strictness, not placeholder cutover: chunks can hold ready semantic text without the exact detailed/brief accounting that strict projection selection expects.

blockingFindings.title: Strict lower-band readiness still diverges from strict semantic accounting and can report ready while omitting lower bands
blockingFindings.evidence: prepareAsyncThread strict mode delegates to readReadiness in src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:1017-1053 and the resulting readiness blocker logic at :882-909 only checks for ready detailed/brief text, not exact detailed/brief token counts. Ready semantic artifacts are persisted without tokenCountMetadata in src/thread/async-thread/services/lower-band-compression-service.ts:716-729, and async maintenance only repairs raw, smooth, projection, and chunk-smooth counts in src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:1583-1610. In strict projection building, resolveChunkSemanticArtifactAccounting falls back to computed heuristic records when persisted exact counts are absent in src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:308-343, and strict selectLowerBandChunkIds simply stops selection when that accounting is unavailable at :523-545. The tests codify the mismatch: tests/thread/async-thread-run-service.test.ts:756-791 accepts canonical semantic chunks without lower-band token metadata, while tests/thread-view/thread-view-builder.test.ts:491-515 expects a strict build to return ready with empty detailed/brief selections for the same canonical semantic chunk shape. That conflicts with the tech-design contract for exact/provider-input semantic lower-band counting in docs/spec-build/epics/05-real-lower-band-compression/tech-design.md:120, :289, and :768-789.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Compaction freshness reporting still treats any ready semantic artifact as fresh
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: inspectLowerBandFreshness in src/workbench/services/compaction-report-service.ts:137-163 returns fresh for any ready artifact text without comparing provenance or prepare-time regeneration, and the report builder at :277-306 just echoes current smooth-source values before recording that fresh status. The suite also asserts degraded-count semantic artifacts as fresh in tests/workbench/compaction-report-service.test.ts:236-278. Because the public report type exposes fresh, regenerated_during_prepare, and blocked_or_stale states, the current implementation cannot distinguish freshly regenerated artifacts from ready-but-stale ones.

unresolvedItems: Either enforce exact/provider-input detailed/brief accounting before strict readiness/build can report ready, or explicitly revise the tech design and strict-mode tests to allow silent lower-band omission.

Decide whether compaction audit freshness is meant to distinguish fresh vs regenerated_during_prepare vs blocked_or_stale in practice, because the public report shape exposes those states but the implementation currently collapses ready artifacts to fresh.

crossStoryFindings: Strict lower-band readiness, strict projection building, and inspection no longer agree on what 'ready' means for semantic lower-band content: async readiness treats ready text as sufficient, while strict projection building silently omits the same chunks when exact semantic counts are absent.

Epic 5 enlarged background `turn_end` maintenance enough to destabilize adjacent lifecycle coverage, so the epic now regresses broader session-lifecycle behavior instead of staying isolated to lower-band stories.

Placeholder fallback removal is mostly consistent across stories: normal runtime selection/build/materialization now consumes semantic `chunk.lowerBand` artifacts, while legacy placeholder state is only blocked, reported, or used by fixtures/tests.
architectureFindings: The tech design defines `resolveChunkSemanticArtifactAccounting` as an exact, per-run, OpenAI-counted boundary, but the implementation is synchronous and falls back to heuristic semantic counts instead of performing the designed exact-count path.

`prepareAsyncThread` strict readiness never validates lower-band count source/trust for selected chunks, so it can approve a thread state that `buildThreadViewProjection` strict mode will not actually materialize into detailed/brief bands.

The builder test suite codifies this drift: strict mode is expected to return `ready` with empty detailed/brief selections when canonical semantic chunks lack exact semantic counts, which conflicts with the design contract for real counted lower-band allocation.
epicCoverageAssessment: Service coverage is broad: conversation-only projections, chunk transcript assembly, retry/escalation, catch-up, placeholder cutover, inspection, and provider-backed lower-band generation all have automated tests.

Coverage around strict counted semantic lower-band allocation is contradictory: the builder suite explicitly expects strict mode to succeed while dropping lower-band selections when exact semantic counts are missing, so the most architecture-sensitive path is both unproven and behaviorally divergent from the design.

Gate coverage is not green: `npm run verify` passed in one run, the `verify` phase inside `npm run verify-all` failed on a flaky service test, and a separate `npm run test:e2e` run failed a long-thread real-runtime proof.
productionPathFindings: No normal runtime caller reaches `ensurePlaceholderArtifacts`; runtime lower-band selection/build/materialization all flow through semantic `chunk.lowerBand` artifacts via `getReadyChunkLowerBandArtifact`.
Legacy placeholder code remains in the repo, but as legacy-state detection/reporting and fixture support rather than as a selectable production fallback.

The strict counted production path is incomplete: lower-band readiness can be reported without exact semantic accounting, so the system can approve or inspect a thread state that the strict projection builder will not actually use for detailed/brief output.

blockingFindings.title: Strict readiness does not enforce the designed exact semantic lower-band accounting path
blockingFindings.evidence: `src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:362-367` and `:415-418` resolve lower-band chunk accounting in `prepare` mode unconditionally, and `:882-909` only blocks missing text, not missing exact semantic counts. The strict builder test at `tests/thread-view/thread-view-builder.test.ts:491-515` then proves the same canonical semantic chunks are silently dropped from strict detailed/brief selection while the build still returns `ready`. This diverges from the exact-count contract described in `docs/spec-build/epics/05-real-lower-band-compression/tech-design.md:768-789`.

blockingFindings.title: The service gate is flaky after lower-band work expanded background turn_end maintenance
blockingFindings.evidence: `npm run verify` exited 0, but the `verify` phase inside `npm run verify-all` exited 1 on `tests/context-steward/pi-smoothing-lifecycle.integration.test.ts:344-383` because `snapshot.thread.status.tokenCounting?.status` stayed undefined for the 10s wait budget. `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:2118-2123` only schedules background maintenance, while `src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:1918-1945` now performs the added Epic 5 repair/counting work in that background path.

blockingFindings.title: The real long-thread runtime proof is not green
blockingFindings.evidence: A separate `npm run test:e2e` run exited 1. In `tests/context-steward/long-thread-real-pi-execution.e2e.test.ts:411-434`, the real PI smoke flow was asked to create and then delete a unique file, but `assertFileDoesNotExist(targetFile)` failed at `:376-382` because the file still existed after the run.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Placeholder runtime code is isolated rather than active
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Repo search shows `ensurePlaceholderArtifacts` is only referenced inside `src/thread/async-thread/services/placeholder-artifact-service.ts` and fixture/test code. Normal runtime lower-band consumers now read semantic artifacts through `getReadyChunkLowerBandArtifact` in `src/thread/async-thread/services/async-thread-run-service.ts:362`, `src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:315`, and `src/thread-view/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:422`.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Compaction freshness reporting does not actually detect stale semantic lower-band artifacts
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `src/workbench/services/compaction-report-service.ts:137-163` marks any ready lower-band artifact as `fresh` and never emits `regenerated_during_prepare`; it only echoes current source values and does not compare artifact provenance against the current transcript/smooth source. That leaves the reporting surface unable to distinguish freshly regenerated summaries from ready-but-stale ones.

unresolvedItems: Decide whether strict smart compact should block on missing exact semantic lower-band counts, or whether the tech design and tests should be updated to explicitly bless silent omission of lower-band bands in strict mode.
Root-cause whether the `pi-smoothing-lifecycle.integration.test.ts` timeout is a true lifecycle regression from expanded background maintenance or an undersized wait budget under full-suite load.
Root-cause whether the long-thread real PI E2E file-deletion miss is runtime/model nondeterminism or a regression in the prepared fixture/runtime harness path.

crossStoryFindings: Epic 5 implementation is cohesive across the projection, chunking, compression, smart-compact, token-accounting, PI output, and workbench/inspection surfaces. Later stories consume the real artifacts created by earlier stories rather than using separate eligibility flags or fake lower-band data.
architectureFindings: The implementation follows the tech-design source chain: canonical messages -> smooth components -> conversation-only turn projection -> chunk transcript -> semantic detailed/brief lower-band artifacts -> projection output.
Chunk state uses the new conversation_only_chunk_v1 canonical path, blocks legacy placeholder chunks from selection, and keeps lower-band selection on semantic lowerBand artifacts.
Smart compact runs prepare-mode repair/catch-up, emits visible lower-band catch-up warnings, blocks on failed selected lower-band generation, and does not write/reload placeholder fallback output.
epicCoverageAssessment: Conversation-only turn projection, projection token counting, chunk boundary counting, transcript assembly, GPT OAuth-backed lower-band compression, retry/escalation behavior, smart-compact readiness/catch-up, placeholder cutover, inspection, and reporting are covered by service, command, provider-backed, and E2E tests.
Story gate npm run verify passed with 491 service tests. Epic gate npm run verify-all passed, including service tests plus E2E/lifecycle tests and long-thread real PI execution coverage.
productionPathFindings: No material fake adapter, shim, placeholder, or non-real lower-band execution path was found in the active compact/build/materialize/PI-output path. Legacy placeholder code remains inspectable/testable as legacy state, but selected production lower-band output is sourced from semantic chunk.lowerBand artifacts and legacy placeholder chunks are blocked.
